title: Shinonome Ena — Luxury Makeup Session〔Part2〕Side Story (Part 2)

rows.Line: Ena's Room

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Let's see... Photography... Composition...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Oh, this site looks helpful.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: The rule of thirds... Frame within a frame...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Again, it's so interesting how you can apply the same composition techniques for both art and photography...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I learned from one of the photography books I bought that taking photos and drawing pictures involve similar techniques.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Really?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Yeah, it even said that it's good to study the works of famous artists.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: I was also surprised when I learned that for the first time. I mean, they even share a lot of the same names.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Actually, it's pretty common for artists to take their own photos and use them to practice, study and improve their composition.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I didn't know that!

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Oh, is that why you take so many selfies? Do they help improve the composition of your drawings?

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Oh, about those...

rows.Speaker: Airi
rows.Line:
They're just for fun.
Ena here craves attention.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: What? Yeah, they're for fun, but I do not crave attention!

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Still, photos, huh...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: I've taken some of the buildings or scenery I want to use later as references.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: But I've never really thought about using photos to study composition.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: You know what, maybe I'll try it out.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Especially if it'll help improve my art.
Nonogi Park

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Alright, I have the path in the distance at the center, and the trees towards the front in frame...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line:
Yeah, not bad...
This gives it a lot of depth.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: But this shadow seems a bit out of place. Where it is now, it's gonna be the first thing people see.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line:
I should've come in the morning...
This shadow was probably in the perfect spot.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: But this still helps a lot, so I'll keep it.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line:
Oh, I forgot...
The pictures I took with my phone of the light poking through those trees turned out really well.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (Which reminds me of that assignment Mr. Yukihira gave me. The one about “light”.)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (He told me that I needed to work on my composition more if I wanted to do my subject justice.)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (And how the way the light peered through looked odd.)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line:
*Sigh*
I wanna redraw it, but I still haven't figured out what's wrong with my composition.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: To be fair, I sorta just winged the lighting for some parts...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Having a picture of something similar would be really helpful. Then, I'd be able to compare it side by side with my piece.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Wait, this was only meant to be a quick test, but it's actually helping a lot...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Alright! Let's try to find some similar trees.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Oh, there was also a pond somewhere around here. I'll snap a few photos of that while I'm here too.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: I came all this way, so I should take as many as I can to get some good references for composition!
